title: Heron's Formula for the 13-14-15 Triangle
originalTopic: Area of a Triangle from Its Sides
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use Heron's formula to compute the exact area of the triangle whose side lengths are 13, 14, and 15.

steps.title: Compute the Semi-perimeter
steps.explanation: Heron's formula works through the semi-perimeter s, half the sum of the three side lengths; here s = 42/2 = 21.
steps.why: The formula A = sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) packages all three sides symmetrically through s, requiring only the perimeter.

steps.title: Form the Three Excess Factors
steps.explanation: Each factor measures how much the semi-perimeter exceeds one side; all three are positive, confirming the triangle is nondegenerate.
steps.why: Positivity of s-a, s-b, s-c is exactly the triangle inequality in disguise, so the radicand is legitimate.

steps.title: Multiply and Take the Square Root
steps.explanation: The product inside the root is 21*8*7*6 = 7056, which is a perfect square: 84 squared equals 7056, so the area is the whole number 84.
steps.why: Factoring as (3*7)*(2^3)*7*(2*3) = 2^4 * 3^2 * 7^2 lets the root extract exactly 2^2*3*7 = 84.
